title: Written in the womb
hookLine: each person is formed in stages, and their provision, lifespan, deeds and end are written
tomorrow: can you add something beautiful to the religion?

cards: Some families keep one on the fridge: a gray, grainy ultrasound printout, a shape you have to squint at. Somebody points. That's the head.
And on the monitor, a heartbeat, fast as a bird's. Yesterday ended on a question: before your first breath, what was already written down?

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud reports the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, describing it. A person is formed in the womb in stages. Then an angel is sent, breathes in the soul, and is told to write four things.

teach.b: The four: provision, lifespan, deeds, and whether the person ends wretched or happy. This is qadar, the decree, the last item on the list of faith the stranger in white asked about. Then the hadith turns hard.

A person can do the deeds of the people of Paradise until only an arm's length is left, and then the writing overtakes them; and the reverse. Stop listening there, and it sounds as if nothing you do matters.
The companions asked about exactly that. In a report in Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet tells them each person's place is already written, and they ask: then shouldn't we rely on it, and stop working?

His answer: act, for each one is made easy for what they were created for. Then he recites from Surah al-Layl, about the one who gives and keeps their duty, whose way is eased. So the writing doesn't replace the effort.
The effort is part of what's written.
Another report in Bukhari adds a small phrase to the arm's-length line: someone does the deeds of Paradise, as it appears to people.
Muslims hold both together: Allah knows and writes, and a person still chooses, strives, and answers for it.

how: Belief in qadar, the decree, is one of the articles of faith Muslims learn from the hadith of Jibril; teachers pair this hadith with the companions' question 'shouldn't we rely on it?' and the answer 'act'.

games.q: what does “written in the womb” mean?
o: a prayer a family says over a newborn baby
what's written for each person before they're born
a promise that a baby will grow up healthy and safe

games.q: what's written, and what to do — tap the pairs.
p: breathes in the soul and writes
shouldn't we just rely on it?

s: the hadith tells people to stop trying, since it's all written
when the companions asked that, the answer was: act, each is made easy for what they were created for.
the angel is told to write provision, lifespan, deeds and the ending
four things, written before a first breath.
qadar covers only the good things that happen
in the hadith of Jibril, faith includes the decree, its good and its bad.

games.q: a friend fails a driving test twice and says, 'maybe it's just not written for me.' what fits today's hadiths?
o: the writing doesn't replace the trying. practice, and take it again.
if it's written, extra lessons won't change what's coming anyway.
only big things are written, so a driving test is all up to you.
games.why: the companions asked the same thing: why work? the answer was act. the effort is part of what's written.

practice: Rest two fingers on the side of your neck, or a hand flat on your chest, until you find your pulse. Let it be the only sound for the sit: it was going before you had a name or did a single thing.
If you pray, you can thank Allah for those first days nobody remembers; if not, just stay with the beat, and be glad of it.

wordCard.voice: Written in the womb: provision, lifespan, deeds and ending, written before a first breath. The decree, qadar, and beside it the word act.

orig.note: Arabic: the decree, what Allah has written for each person.

carryVoice: To carry today: written, and still we strive, the way the companions were told to act. Six days into the last range.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3208; Sahih Muslim 2643 (Ibn Mas'ud: formed in stages; the angel writes provision, lifespan, deeds, wretched or happy; the arm's length)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4949; Sahih Muslim 2647 (Ali: 'shall we not rely on what is written?' 'Act, for each is eased toward what he was created for'; Qur'an 92:5–7 recited)
Sahih al-Bukhari 2898; Sahih Muslim 112 (deeds of the people of Paradise 'as it appears to people')
